applies_why: The judge text makes an UNDERDETERMINED call about Luke 2:48-49 and rests it on the relation between two father-references in that verse, so K-S2 governs the call.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The phrase "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand" was read either as allowing UNDERDETERMINED when two father-references appear, or as forbidding that because both senses stand and the verse is not open.
why: The judge assigns UNDERDETERMINED on the basis of the verse's two father-references, which K-S2 forbids because a verse with two senses at once is not open and both senses stand.
